dedupe_keys.name: participatory benefit cost analysis of opening the fadura green space getxo spain

description: This study developed a framework for the economic benefits and costs of public interventions that give citizens access to urban green spaces, using the Thinking Fadura project in Getxo, Spain, as its case. A participatory benefit-cost analysis combined a stakeholder-driven evaluation with a standard cost-benefit analysis, following a bottom-up sequence through key stakeholders and experts, visitors and the general public. Coverage: the Fadura site in Getxo. Access: open-access article in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (2020). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: valuation rests on stated preferences and assumptions specific to one site. Outcome: benefits outweighed costs, the largest being amenity and recreational value and increased physical activity, and the participatory evaluation highlighted what access meant to people. Simulation uses: parameters for appraising park access investments. Related records: the Peterborough park health valuation and the Barcelona superblocks evaluation.
